name: Email Blast Replies -> Replies Tab
_comment: LIVE as workflow vrqDhZprQ0TgwPdS in the n8n project 'John Luiz Gonzaga <john@callplaybook.com>'.
Created INACTIVE on purpose: activating before EMAIL_REPLY_SECRET is set in Vercel means every
It had to live in John's own project because n8n refuses a credential from another project, and
the Gmail credential must be the mailbox the +q return address delivers to.
NO GMAIL LABEL OR FILTER IS NEEDED - the trigger's own Gmail query does the narrowing, and the
code node enforces the +q tag as a second guard.
THE MAILBOX IS READ ONLY. Never add a Gmail send, reply or draft node to this workflow.

nodes.name: Gmail: blast replies
nodes.notes: READ ONLY. Never attach a Gmail send/reply/draft node to this credential. Must be john@callplaybook.com - the mailbox the +q return address delivers to. simple:false is REQUIRED: the simplified output drops headers, and the +q tag lives on a recipient header. readStatus:both because a reply a human has already opened still needs ingesting; the trigger only fetches messages newer than its last poll, and the endpoint dedupes on Gmail message id, so nothing is posted twice.

nodes.name: Extract + Require +q Tag
nodes.notes: Returns null for anything without a +q tag, which drops the item. That is the safety net keeping personal mail out of the app.

nodes.name: POST /api/email-reply
nodes.notes: Credential is a HEADER AUTH: Name 'x-reply-secret', Value = the same string as EMAIL_REPLY_SECRET in Vercel. One static header, so Header Auth fits exactly — 'Custom Auth' in the n8n picker is a different credential type (httpCustomAuth) and will not attach to this node. Errors are NOT swallowed: a failed write should fail the execution so it is visible and retried. The endpoint dedupes on Gmail message id, so a retry cannot double-post.
